title: Halal Cart Chicken and Rice
summary: Spiced, harissa-marinated chicken thigh pieces seared until charred, over turmeric-cumin rice cooked in stock, with lettuce, salted tomatoes, a creamy white sauce and a mellow red chili sauce.
notes: Video: 'Halal Guys Chicken And Rice But Better' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/halal-guys-chicken-over-rice-but-better-recipe (serves 6, prep 30 min, cook 45 min, plus optional overnight marinating). The video states almost every amount. Where the two differ, the video wins: MSG in the rice is 1/2 tsp in the video, 1 tsp in the written recipe. From the written recipe: the word 'harissa' in the marinade (the captions drop it), 3 Roma tomatoes, 1 head of iceberg. Our estimate: 2 Tbsp oil for searing in batches. Both sauces are counted in full, as if every serving gets its share; he says to go lighter on the red sauce, so real intake is probably lower. Not counted: salt and pepper 'to taste' in the sauces, the oil and salt on the tomatoes (no amount), and the optional pita. Smoked paprika uses USDA paprika; chiles de árbol use USDA sun-dried hot chile. Harissa uses a branded harissa paste record (USDA FDC 2546030), MSG a branded MSG record.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into 1/2-3/4 inch pieces. Add the salt, spices, oregano, lemon juice and harissa and knead until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate overnight (up to 2 days), or cook right away.

Rinse the basmati 2-3 times until the water runs clear, level it, add the turmeric, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, MSG and salt, then an equal volume of chicken stock. Stir and start the rice cooker.

Red sauce: boil the chiles de árbol in the water for 3-4 minutes, until soft. Blend them with their water, the harissa, smoked paprika, sugar, vinegar, garlic and salt until smooth. Strain if you like, and adjust the salt.
White sauce: whisk the mayo, sour cream, sugar, MSG, salt, lemon juice, vinegar, grated garlic and black pepper. Adjust the seasoning.
Core the tomatoes, dice them 1/2 inch, and toss with a little salt and olive oil.
Sear the chicken in batches in a hot pan with a little oil, in one layer: 2-3 minutes undisturbed, then flip, lower to medium and cook through to 165°F.
Grate a clove of garlic over the cooked chicken and toss.
Fluff the rice with the cubed cold butter until it melts in.
Serve the rice topped with chicken, shredded lettuce and tomatoes, drizzled with white sauce and, more lightly, red sauce. Pita on the side if you like.
